name: Pilate
note: Luke's trial narrative (23:1-25) shows a Pilate who tries three times to release Jesus. Josephus's Pilate — who sneaks Caesar's images into Jerusalem by night and later slaughters Samaritans, the incident that gets him recalled to Rome — is a harder, more provocative administrator, the reputation Luke's crowd would have already known him by. Philo tells a separate incident — gilded shields in Herod's old palace, no images, just an inscription — that Tiberius himself ordered taken down after Jewish protest, a second, independent witness to the same abrasive governorship.
